title: Tree Traversal Techniques
description: Techniques to visit every node in a binary tree in a systematic way.
identify: The problem requires visiting all nodes in a specific order.
The problem asks for DFS (Preorder, Inorder, Postorder) or BFS (Level Order).
explanation: Traversals form the foundation of all tree algorithms. They dictate the order in which we access and process nodes.

title: Tree Properties
description: Algorithms that determine the structural properties of a binary tree.
identify: The problem asks for height, diameter, or width.
The problem requires checking symmetry, balance, or identical structures.
explanation: These problems generally rely on Postorder traversal (Bottom-Up approach), where we compute properties of subtrees first and then combine them at the parent.

title: Tree Views
description: Visualizing the tree from different perspectives (Top, Bottom, Left, Right).
identify: The problem asks for the outer boundary or visible nodes from a specific angle.
explanation: Views typically rely on Level Order Traversal (BFS) combined with a horizontal distance map or a depth map to track the first or last node seen at each position.

title: Path-Related Problems
description: Finding or analyzing paths between nodes in a tree.
identify: The problem asks for a path from root to leaf.
The problem asks for a path sum or distance between any two nodes.
explanation: Paths are explored using Preorder traversal (Top-Down) while passing the current path state down to children.

title: Tree Ancestor Problems
description: Problems focused on finding common ancestors or relationships between distant nodes.
identify: The problem requires finding the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA).
The problem asks for the distance or relationship between a node and its ancestors.
explanation: Ancestor problems often use a Bottom-Up traversal to bubble up matching nodes to their common parent.

title: Tree Constructions
description: Building or modifying the structure of a tree based on specific rules or traversals.
identify: The problem provides two traversals (e.g., Inorder + Preorder) and asks to build the tree.
The problem asks to flatten or mutate the tree.
explanation: Construction uses a recursive Divide and Conquer strategy, identifying the root first, and then recursively building the left and right subtrees.

title: Serialize and Deserialize
description: Converting a tree into a string or array format and vice versa.
identify: The problem asks to save a tree to a file or transmit it over a network.
explanation: Serialization typically relies on Preorder or Level Order traversal, ensuring that NULL nodes are explicitly marked so the tree can be unambiguously reconstructed.
